_comment: HTTP variant of .mcp.json — point Claude Code (or any MCP client) at the remote
eme-gir.recoverysky.org reverse-proxied endpoints instead of spawning local stdio subprocesses.
Each per-domain MCP server is reachable at https://eme-gir.recoverysky.org/<server>/mcp,
served by the corresponding container in docker-compose.yml (ports 5052-5056) behind a TLS-
terminating reverse proxy (caddy/nginx/traefik). No local Python install needed on the client side.
If the deployment enables EME_GIR_REQUIRE_AUTH=1, attach a bearer token via the client's auth config
(Auth0 RS256 JWT scoped to the configured Auth0 tenant); see eme_gir/auth0_verifier.py for the contract.
To swap to local stdio, use .mcp.json instead — both files describe the same five servers and same tools.

eme-gir-epsd2._comment: ePSD2 dictionary + corpus tools — the biggest data server, the primary surface for English ↔ Sumerian translation.
_tools: start_here              ⭐ returns the EPSD2_PROMPT bootstrap doc (sense ranking, period filters, slot grammar). CALL FIRST.
translate_english       English word → ranked Sumerian candidates with sense_count + sense_pct
lookup_entry            full structured view of a dictionary entry (senses, spellings, periods, compounds)
see_examples            real attested corpus lines for an entry, with CDLI links + museum metadata
find_compound           Sumerian compounds (multi-word cf AND orthographic) matching an English phrase
get_inflections         show attested morphological breakdowns for a lemma
analyze_form            decompose a Sumerian spelling into candidate lemmas + morphological role
translate_sumerian      Sumerian transliteration → per-token English glosses + suffix detection
parse_phrase            case-aware grammatical pre-annotation with bracket skeleton
find_collocations       multi-word phrasal idioms attested with a given lemma (2/3/4-grams)
find_phrase_pattern     structural template query with TARGET[gw]:case slot grammar
find_verb_form          attestation-first verb-form retrieval by grammatical feature spec

eme-gir-etcsl._comment: ETCSL Oxford literary corpus — 394 lemmatized literary texts with English translations. ⚠️ ATTRIBUTION REQUIRED (CC BY 3.0 UK) — every response carries an `attribution` field; pass it through verbatim.
_tools: start_here              ⭐ returns the ETCSL_PROMPT bootstrap doc (text-id conventions, FTS5 syntax, attribution rule). CALL FIRST.
etcsl_search_english    FTS5 search over Oxford English translations; returns bilingual hits (Sumerian + English)
etcsl_lines_with_lemma  find literary lines containing a Sumerian lemma (cf), each with its English paragraph
etcsl_lookup_text       read a whole composition; paged via ord (line ordinal, not line label)
etcsl_search_sumerian   FTS5 search over Sumerian transliterations in ETCSL

eme-gir-cdli._comment: CDLI artifact catalogue — 353K cuneiform-bearing objects with provenience, museum custody, dimensions, photo/lineart URLs. Snapshot date August 2022, CC0.
_tools: start_here              ⭐ returns the CDLI_PROMPT bootstrap doc (filter enums, URL rendering rules, Royal/Monumental gotcha). CALL FIRST.
lookup_artifact         full CDLI record for one P-id (designation, period, provenience, museum, image URLs)
find_artifacts          filtered query by provenience / period / museum_collection / genre / language (all substring-matched)

eme-gir-ogsl._comment: OGSL cuneiform sign rendering — the Oracc Global Sign List, ~3,000+ signs with Unicode codepoints and cross-language readings (Sumerian, Akkadian, Hittite, Hurrian, Elamite).
_tools: start_here              ⭐ returns the OGSL_PROMPT bootstrap doc (transliteration conventions, □ placeholder semantics). CALL FIRST.
cuneify                 convert Oracc-style transliteration into Unicode cuneiform glyphs (𒈗𒂊 𒂍 𒈬𒈾𒆕)
lookup_sign             look up a sign by name (LUGAL) or phonetic value (lugal/šarru); returns glyph + all readings + codepoint

eme-gir-translator._comment: Bootstrap surface only — agent prompt + dual-register Sumerian grammar reference. NO data tools. Composes with the four data MCPs above.
_tools: start_here              ⭐ returns the AGENT_PROMPT — recommended end-to-end English ↔ Sumerian workflow across all five servers
get_grammar_reference   returns the dual Jagersma (academic) + Meadow (temple register) Sumerian grammar (~80 KB combined)
